To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) we have developed a system that is able to retrieve a passage from a MIDI file given a cell phone picture taken of a sheet music page and b) the system has no trainable weights and does not require training on any data.

a) a cell phone picture can be used to retrieve music from a large MIDI database, b) the retrieval performance is competitive with state-of-the art commercial optical music recognition systems, c) the retrieval performance can be improved using a mid level feature called a bootleg representation, and d) our system is the first to solve this problem.
we introduce a mid-level representation of sheet music called the bootleg score and that we show that it can be used in a cell phone based music retrieval system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel retrieval scenario and we present a novel mid level feature representation and an algorithm for retrieving a passage of music by taking a picture of a physical sheet of paper.
a new retrieval problem, introduces a new feature representation called a "bootleg score", and proposes a simple and effective system to solve the problem using a novel feature representation.
a new retrieval problem, introduces a new mid level representation for music, and presents an algorithm for cross modal retrieval using this representation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our system is the first to address the problem of MIDI passage retrieval using cell phone pictures of sheet music and that it achieves state of the art results.
we have developed a new system that can retrieve MIDI music passages from cell phone pictures of sheet music with an accuracy that is competitive with commercial optical recognition software.
this paper investigates a cross-modal retrieval problem in which the user would like to query a passage of MIDI music by taking a cell-phone picture of the sheet music.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are the first to introduce a cross-modal music retrieval system that is based on a deterministic representation of sheet music, and that we achieve state of the art results in a novel retrieval scenario.
we have shown that a system that does not use any trainable weights can achieve a reasonable performance on this problem.
we have developed a system for cross modal music information retrieval which is simple and robust and can be implemented using only off the shelf components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rules of Western music notation can be used to solve the cross modal retrieval problem.
the use of a mid level representation that explicitly encodes musical notation is a viable strategy for solving this cross modal retrieval problem.

a simple deterministic system can achieve high accuracy on the retrieval task, and that a system that can perform test time adaptation is more robust to noise in the query than a system that is fully supervised.
